Here’s a classic set of ingredients you’ll need to make a traditional meat‑based lasagna (serves about 8 people):

**For the meat sauce (Bolognese):**
- 2 lb (≈ 900 g) ground beef (or a mix of beef and pork)
- 1 lb (≈ 450 g) ground pork (optional, for richer flavor)
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2–3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, finely diced
- 1 celery stalk, finely diced
- 1 cup (≈ 240 ml) dry red wine (optional, but adds depth)
- 1 can (28 oz / 796 ml) crushed tomatoes or whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried basil
- ½ tsp dried thyme
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2–3 tbsp olive oil (for sautéing)

**For the béchamel sauce (white sauce):**
- 4 Tbsp (≈ 60 g) unsalted butter
- ⅓ cup (≈ 40 g) all‑purpose flour
- 4 cups (≈ 950 ml) whole milk, warmed
- Pinch of nutmeg (freshly grated, optional)
- Salt and white pepper, to taste

**Other components:**
- 12–15 lasagna sheets (no‑boil or regular, depending on your preference)
- 2 cups (≈ 200 g) shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1 cup (≈ 100 g) grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 cup (≈ 100 g) ricotta cheese (optional, for a creamier layer)
- Fresh basil or parsley, chopped (for garnish)

**Optional extras:**
- ½ cup (≈ 120 ml) heavy cream (to enrich the béchamel)
- 1 tsp dried rosemary or bay leaf (for added aroma)
- ½ cup (≈ 120 ml) grated Pecorino Romano (for sharper flavor)
- 1–2 tbsp capers or olives (for a briny twist)

Feel free to adjust quantities or add your own touches—lasagna is wonderfully adaptable!
